subject: AWS Private Offer — pricing anchor and cross-account approval path
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Kerry Huang <kerry.huang@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS Private Offer — pricing anchor and cross-account approval path

Hi Kerry,

Thanks again for the time earlier — really enjoyed the product deep-dive. Per our conversation here are two pragmatic private-offer paths we can take so procurement/CFO have a simple decision: 

Option A — Short pilot (recommended)
- 3-month pilot on Marketplace private offer at list MRR with a conversion credit if converted to an annual ELA within 90 days.
- Conversion economics: we propose a 30% conversion credit applied as prepaid credits against the first year once signed.
- Minimal evidence pack (SOC 2 summary, network diagram, billing proof) to speed CFO review.

Option B — Annual commit (fastest for activation)
- 12-month commitment placed as an AWS Private Offer. 15–25% pricing anchor depending on commit size and co-sell credits.
- Standard buyer approval path (may require CFO signature and procurement PO).

Risks and gating
- Marketplace private-offer activation can be delayed if buyer finance requires full procurement review. Cross-account activation (seller-assisted activation) reduces lag — we can enable this if ACME grants a limited activation role to our marketplace admin.
- Anything >$250k will typically trigger CFO review at ACME (per Kerry’s note).

Action items I need from you to design the PO:
1) Confirm preference (Pilot vs Annual) and target dollar value or monthly burn estimate.
2) Procurement contact (if different from Anil) and their PO cadence.

Attaching a quick pricing model and a PO template for your legal/procurement folks to review. If useful I can also produce a one-page CFO summary that lists only the evidence your finance team typically needs.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: pricing-model-v3.xlsx, PO-template.docx

Date: 2027-04-27T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — pricing anchor and cross-account approval path

Soojin — thanks, this is helpful.

Short answers:
- We’d prefer Option A (3-month pilot) to limit initial procurement hoops. If the pilot demonstrates value we’ll convert to an annual ELA.
- Anil is procurement lead (copied). CFO will want a one-page summary with clear cost/benefit and a minimal evidence list.
- Can you confirm the conversion credit mechanics in writing (how it shows up on invoice / how credits are applied)? Procurement will need that detail.

If you can provide a one-page CFO summary and the conversion-credit clause, I can push this through our internal fast-track review.

— Kerry
Director, Clinical AI | Acme Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — pricing anchor and cross-account approval path

Soojin / Vivek — quick internal note with recommended approach based on Kerry’s ask:

Recommended: 3-month pilot via Marketplace private offer + conversion credit (pilot -> annual)
- Mechanics: create private offer for 3 months of committed credits (invoice on Marketplace). Include a contract addendum: if customer signs full-year ELA within 90 days of pilot completion we apply a 30% credit equal to the pilot spend to their AWS invoice as prepaid credits. We’ve used this structure with two other healthcare buyers and it shows as a credit allocation on the Marketplace billing line (procurement-friendly).
- Approval gating: to minimize CFO friction, produce a one-page summary that includes: total pilot cost, conversion credit language, SOC 2 attestation, KMS + encryption note, and a one-line integration timeline. That last piece helps CFO understand ramp risk.
- Cross-account activation: proposal — ask Kerry to grant our marketplace activation role for the specific Private Offer (timeboxed). This avoids back-and-forth and reduces activation latency from weeks to 48–72 hours. If they prefer not to grant role, the PO still works but expect a 7–14 day activation lag depending on procurement windows.

I’ve exported a short evidence checklist to the drive link below. I’ll draft the one-page CFO summary and the formal conversion-credit clause for legal to sign off.

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-evidence

Jordan Blake
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-pack.zip

Subject: RE: AWS Private Offer — pricing anchor and cross-account approval path

Kerry / Anil — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

1) We will proceed with Option A — 3-month pilot private offer.
- I’ll prepare the Marketplace private-offer request and include the conversion-credit clause Jordan outlined (30% credit against first-year invoice if ELA executed within 90 days of pilot).

2) Evidence pack and CFO one-pager
- Jordan has uploaded the checklist and I’ll circulate a one-page CFO summary in the next 24 hours that lists only the items your finance team needs: SOC 2 type II summary, brief network diagram, KMS/HSM note, billing sample. Link above.

3) Activation preference
- We recommend cross-account activation to speed things up. If ACME is comfortable, please grant marketplace activation access for the private-offer ID once I send it (timeboxed to 5 days). If not, we’ll coordinate with Anil on the procurement activation steps — expect an additional 7–10 day lead.

4) Procurement send
- Once you confirm Anil (procurement) is the correct PO recipient, I’ll send a filled PO-template and the exact Marketplace offer lines for them to approve.

Proposed calendar: I’ll send the CFO one-pager by 4/29; we can aim to have the pilot active by 5/6 if activation is cross-account.

Appreciate the quick sync — looping Jordan/Vivek for visibility.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
